analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation-only edits to docs/architecture/inference.md. The visible patch hunks describe out-of-order performance observations (head ~872-878) and TTFT admission estimator corrections (head ~1122-1158), plus a one-line change near 2073. The units I received are head_text lines 1-797 and the patch excerpt, which is truncated and does not include the later hunks. I treated the head text as largely pre-existing context.

The hunk text I could see makes no behavior changes. It documents rate freshness anchoring, i.e. age/expiry anchored to the newest observation. It also documents per-batch-step decode charging, with an env toggle DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 to restore the old estimators. Security relevance is limited: these are provider-local admission and deadline estimators and heartbeat performance evidence. They touch availability (the DoS-style threats around admission and capacity) but not the key, attestation, encryption or authorization boundaries. The doc says a heartbeat snapshot alone never renews evidence, which is a conservative statement.

The long Nemotron, GLM and prefix-cache text in the head excerpt describes existing designs. It mentions text prefix reuse partitioned by authenticated cache scope, and off without one. This is consistent with T-041 scoping and shows no weakening. No TTL, scope, KEK or lookup-tag changes are visible.

Residual question: the actual source (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift) is not supplied. The behavior it implements, such as step-cost scaling, could under-estimate load and over-admit. That cannot be judged from docs, so it is left to the source passes. I found no concrete regression and no threat-model gap from these doc changes.
